stories.title: US Army Secretary Daniel Driscoll submits resignation, media reports say
stories.summary: Army secretary’s resignation follows months of tensions with US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, US media reports say. United States Army Secretary Daniel Driscoll has submitted his resignation following months of tension with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, according to media reports. Asked about a Wall Street Journal report on Driscoll’s resignation on Monday, the White House did not deny it. “Secretary Driscoll has been highly effective in advancing President Trump’s agenda to Make America Strong Again at the Department of the Army by providing outstanding leadership during historic military operations, restoring an emphasis on readiness and lethality, assisting with negotiations between Russia and Ukraine, and more,” Spokeswoman Anna Kelly said in a statement. “The United States Army is more powerful than ever thanks to his work alongside the Commander-in-Chief and Secretary of War,” she added. The Reuters news agency, citing a source familiar with the matter, said it was unclear whether the White House has accepted Driscoll’s resignation. The Army declined to comment. Driscoll, who is considered close to US Vice President JD Vance, is the latest senior official to leave the Pentagon under Hegseth. In April, Hegseth fired US Army Chief of Staff Randy George in a major staffing change at the Pentagon.

stories.title: New super flu vaccine rollout begins as NHS regroups from 'busiest summer'
stories.summary: This winter's flu vaccine has been updated to protect against last year's Super-K strain, with the first doses being given to schoolchildren and pregnant women. Flu hit early last winter, with a new mutated version of the virus circulating - a seasonal influenza called subclade K or Super-K. School children are being prioritised - and like pregnant women can get the jab from Tuesday - because they can catch and spread flu easily. Protecting them also helps others, including baby brothers or sisters and grandparents. Other eligible groups, including people aged 65 and over, can get a free NHS flu shot from October and should receive an invite by phone or post. Last winter's flu season was unexpected, beginning more than a month earlier than usual, external with the Super-K strain. Super flu is not a medical term, and it does not mean the virus has become harder to treat, just that people are yet to build up immunity against it. Flu vaccines are updated annually to ensure they are a good match for the type of flu circulating. Influenza viruses constantly mutate and experts have to predict these changes ahead of time. This year's vaccine has had a few tweaks, including one to better match subclade K. It is not clear when flu will hit this year, and whether it will be a bad season. But experts often look to southern hemisphere countries, like Australia and New Zealand, to gain a better understanding of how the UK could be affected.

stories.title: Summer 2026 expected to be declared UK's hottest on record
stories.summary: The Met Office is expected to confirm that the UK has had its hottest summer since records began in 1884. Provisional figures for the months of June, July and August are due to be released on Tuesday afternoon and are likely to reveal that mean temperatures - which include daytime and overnight values - have broken the previous record, set just last year. It follows a spring and summer of persistent heat with five widespread heatwaves and 40 days of temperatures above 30C (86F), smashing the previous record of 34 days. The temperature figures are in line with evidence that summers are getting hotter, with more intense and frequent heatwaves, as a result of human-induced climate change. Records are being broken more often - and by bigger margins. For much of the summer, areas of high pressure have dominated the UK weather, with dry conditions and winds from continental Europe allowing temperatures to rise repeatedly. On 11 August the Met Office said it was looking increasingly likely to be the hottest summer since records began. The UK's mean temperature for the summer up to that point stood at 16.48C (61.66F), with only average conditions needed during the remainder of August to confirm the seasonal record. The second half of the month did bring a change in the pattern with cooler, wetter weather for many - but overall temperatures have mostly remained around or above the seasonal norm. Some variations are expected in the final figures for the four UK nations. England and Wales are both expected to set new records, Northern Ireland is likely to come close - but Scotland will fall short. The highest temperature recorded this summer was 38.1C (100.6F) at Kew Gardens in London on 13 August.
